newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natural gas prices ease in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natural gas prices ease in quiet trade.

text.p: Most Canadian spot natural gas prices for August eased from week-ago levels in quiet Wednesday trade with marketers expecting prices to fall a few more cents in September.

Gas for August delivery at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was talked in the C$1.14/1.145 per gigajoule range, up from C$1.17/1.18 last week. September AECO gas was quoted around $1.13 per GJ, down about two cents.
"Everything's pretty flat right now," said a Calgary-based trader. "In September, things should soften a bit. It's a shoulder month."

He said he expected prices to be further pressured by a TransCanada PipeLines Ltd maintenance window running from September 3-28, which is expected to back about 350 million cubic feet per day of gas into Alberta.
At the borders, Export gas at Monchy, Saskatchewan and Emerson, Manitoba was talked over US$0.30 per million British thermal units down from last week as temperatures in the U.S. Midwest moderated.
"It's a dead market," said one Canadian trader of Midwest gas. Prices for the September bid week ended at about US$1.60 per mmBtu for gas at Ventura, after starting in the US$1.80s.
The trader said he expected prices to be a little stronger in the September aftermarket. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
